headline: ABC rates six Senate races toss-ups with control at stake
summary: ABC News rates Texas, Alaska, Ohio, Kansas, Maine and Iowa as toss-ups and Michigan as Lean Democrat; Democrats need a net gain of four seats to win the chamber.

headline: Peltola asks judge to dismiss DOJ certification suit
summary: Mary Peltola and the DSCC asked U.S. District Judge Sharon Gleason to throw out the Justice Department suit that could block certification if Sen. Dan Sullivan narrowly loses. No ruling date has been set.

headline: Prop A opponents dominate as voters weigh 2025 map
summary: A yes vote on Proposition A would put Missouri's 2025 congressional map, which targets Rep. Emanuel Cleaver's district, into effect by 2028; a no vote keeps the 2022 lines. The no side is running ads statewide while organized support for the measure is scarce.

headline: Data centers become a closing issue in Ohio governor race
summary: Amy Acton and Vivek Ramaswamy are trading ads over data centers in the final week, with Acton backing a conditional moratorium. AdImpact data show about $79 million more in ad spending for Ramaswamy than for Acton.

headline: Tariffs weigh on Republicans in the final stretch
summary: GOP candidates are defending Trump's tariffs while seeking relief from parts that hurt their states, and the White House exempted some Canadian goods after pressure from Sen. Susan Collins. Recent Pew and AP-NORC polling shows waning confidence in the tariffs.

headline: DGA adds $5 million for Bottoms in Georgia
summary: The Democratic Governors Association put another $5 million into Keisha Lance Bottoms's campaign, on top of $11.5 million earlier. Republican Rick Jackson leads by single digits in polling averages in a race Cook rates a toss-up.

headline: Early vote passes 30 million a week before Election Day
summary: More than 30 million Americans had voted early as of Oct. 26, per the University of Florida Election Lab. Early turnout is running well above 2022 in Texas, Maine and Ohio but slightly below it in Iowa.

headline: Democratic super PAC spends in Trump-won House seats
summary: House Majority PAC spent about $2.2 million against Rep. Brad Finstad in Minnesota's 1st District and about $380,000 against Rep. Victoria Spartz in Indiana's 5th. GOP groups have shifted money among other House districts.

headline: Redrawn GOP districts turn into costly toss-ups
summary: Several seats Republicans redrew to favor themselves, including North Carolina's 1st District with over $42 million in ads, are now competitive. Two redrawn Florida districts are nearing $90 million in combined ad spending.

headline: Hochul and Blakeman clash on costs as NY early voting opens
summary: New York's early voting runs through Nov. 1, and Gov. Kathy Hochul and Republican Bruce Blakeman are focusing on affordability and utility bills. Blakeman is pitching an income tax exemption on the first $50,000 of income for single filers.

headline: Blanche: DOJ could step in on certification if law requires
summary: On Face the Nation, Attorney General Todd Blanche said counting and certification should proceed normally but the Justice Department could intervene if the facts and law require it. He declined to describe his conversations with Trump about the Alaska case.

headline: Rogers says he never called El-Sayed a terrorist
summary: Michigan Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers said he has never called Democrat Abdul El-Sayed a terrorist, distancing himself from Trump's rhetoric about his opponent. Obama rallied for El-Sayed in Detroit on Saturday as Michigan's early voting began.

headline: What each midterm outcome would mean for Trump's last two years
summary: Republicans hold the House 218-214 and the Senate 53-47; polls favor Democrats for the House while the Senate is seen as too close to call. A Democratic House would gain subpoena power, while Senate control mainly decides judicial and cabinet confirmations.

headline: Peltola hurt in car crash, reschedules Alaska events
summary: Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola and her family suffered minor injuries when another driver struck their vehicle on the way to the Alaska Federation of Natives banquet. On medical advice she is rescheduling Sunday and Monday events and delaying the start of a statewide tour.

headline: Blanche defends DOJ suit over Alaska Senate certification
summary: On CNN's State of the Union, Attorney General Todd Blanche said the Justice Department's suit, which seeks to block certification if Sen. Dan Sullivan loses, is meant to prevent voter confusion over a second Sullivan on the ballot, not to overturn results. Peltola called the suit corrupt and Sen. Lisa Murkowski criticized it.

headline: Trump heads to Port Huron for Rogers as Obama backs Nixon in Florida
summary: Trump was scheduled to rally Sunday in Port Huron, Michigan, for Senate nominee Mike Rogers, an event expected to touch on the U.S.-Canada tariff dispute that has hit the auto industry. Separately, Obama endorsed Democrat Angie Nixon in Florida's Senate race against GOP Sen. Ashley Moody.

headline: Amendment 3's exceptions draw scrutiny from doctors and lawyers
summary: Amendment 3 would repeal the 2024 abortion-rights amendment and restore a ban with exceptions for medical emergencies, certain fetal anomalies, and rape or incest up to 12 weeks. Physicians and attorneys say the language may be hard to apply, and it is unclear whether clinics could provide even the exempted abortions given pending court rulings.

headline: DOJ to send poll monitors to six Georgia counties
summary: The Justice Department plans to monitor voting in Bibb, Chatham, Cobb, DeKalb, Fulton and Gwinnett counties, all Democratic-leaning. It follows the department's announcement of about 1,000 observers nationwide.

headline: Maricopa County restores 24 citizens' voter registrations
summary: Arizona AG Kris Mayes and Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap settled a lawsuit through mediation, restoring active status for 24 voters who had been flagged as possible noncitizens but were found to be citizens. Mayes dropped the suit but maintains Heap lacked authority to inactivate them.

headline: DOJ goes to Ninth Circuit over 20,000 California mail ballots
summary: The Justice Department appealed to the Ninth Circuit before a federal judge had ruled on its request to set aside mail ballots from more than 20,000 California voters it says are likely noncitizens. California disputes the claim and calls the appeal premature; arguments on the restraining order are set for Oct. 27.

headline: Trump touts Audi plant in Georgia; Kemp extends gas-tax suspension
summary: At a rally in Perry, Trump announced a $4.2 billion Audi plant in Middle Georgia alongside GOP governor nominee Rick Jackson, who faces Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms in a close race. Gov. Brian Kemp skipped the rally and extended the state gas-tax suspension through Nov. 30.

headline: Paxton and Talarico rally Central Texas during early voting
summary: Republican Ken Paxton held a rally in Georgetown while Democrat James Talarico campaigned at UT Austin, as record spending continues in Texas's open Senate race. Early voting runs through Oct. 30.

headline: Cruz joins Paxton as Texas race stays tied
summary: Sen. Ted Cruz rallied with Ken Paxton against James Talarico; a Fox News poll this week had them tied at 49%.

headline: Trump rallies in Georgia for Collins and Jackson
summary: At a rally in Perry, Trump backed Senate nominee Mike Collins and governor nominee Rick Jackson and announced a planned Audi plant in Macon.

headline: Obama campaigns in Cleveland and Detroit
summary: Barack Obama rallied for Ohio Democrats Sherrod Brown and Amy Acton, then for Michigan Democrats Abdul El-Sayed and Jocelyn Benson.

headline: Iowa Senate average tips to Hinson
summary: Two straight polls show Republican Ashley Hinson ahead, moving the RealClearPolling average to Hinson +0.6 over Democrat Josh Turek. Kansas's average also sits at Marshall +0.3.

headline: Nearly $60 million flows into Missouri ballot measure fights
summary: Missouri ballot measure campaigns have raised about $59.6 million since 2025, led by almost $26 million for the opponents of Amendment 3. The report also tracks spending in the 2nd Congressional District, competitive state Senate seats and the state auditor's race, where Republican Scott Fitzpatrick far outraised Democrat Quentin Wilson.

headline: Cook shifts 19 House races toward Democrats
summary: The Cook Political Report moved 19 House races toward Democrats and now projects a Democratic gain of 12 to 22 seats. It rates 220 seats as at least leaning Democratic, above the 218 needed for a majority.

headline: Cook moves Ohio governor's race to Lean Democrat
summary: The Cook Political Report shifted Ohio's governor race from Toss Up to Lean Democrat for Amy Acton after backlash to Vivek Ramaswamy's ad featuring Acton's estranged mother. Sabato's Crystal Ball had made a similar move a day earlier.

headline: DDHQ forecast: Democrats favored for House, edge in Senate
summary: Decision Desk HQ's model gives Democrats a 79% chance to win the House and 57% for the Senate.

headline: Democrats outraise GOP Senate candidates in early October
summary: Talarico raised $17.6M to Paxton's $2.8M in Oct 1–14, and El-Sayed raised $8.7M to Rogers's $2.5M. The GOP-aligned Senate Leadership Fund still has $88M in the bank, the most of any Senate group.

headline: North Carolina early vote tops 1.1 million as Cooper rallies
summary: After one week of early voting, about 1.1 million North Carolinians had voted, 38% more than at the same point in 2022, with unaffiliated turnout up 72%. Democrat Roy Cooper, who has led Republican Michael Whatley in polls for the open Senate seat, rallied supporters in Raleigh.

headline: Maine poll: Collins and Jackson tied at 49%
summary: A Fox News poll of 1,514 likely voters (Oct. 16-20) found Sen. Susan Collins and Democrat Troy Jackson tied, with Collins leading independents by 13 points. Democrat Hannah Pingree led the governor's race by 10 points.

headline: Georgia governor's race a dead heat in AJC/UGA poll
summary: Republican Rick Jackson had 46% and Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms 45% among 1,000 likely voters surveyed Oct. 7-15, within the 3.1-point margin of error. Bottoms led independents 43% to 38%.

headline: Pennsylvania Democrats requesting fewer mail ballots
summary: About 1.2 million Pennsylvanians had been approved for mail ballots as of Oct. 19, with Democratic requests down 14% from 2022 while Republican requests rose 11%. Experts said the data can't show whether Trump's blocked mail-voting order caused the drop.

headline: Under-the-radar House races shift toward Democrats
summary: Most of the lesser-watched House races Punchbowl flagged in September have moved toward Democrats, with GOP groups cutting ad spending in seats such as New York's 3rd and Nevada's 3rd. Democrats are now competing in redder seats including Florida's 22nd, Wisconsin's 1st and Kentucky's 6th.

headline: Martin and Brewer make final push in House District 44
summary: Republican Rep. John Martin faces Democrat Bekki Brewer in Boone County's only contested Missouri House race, covering parts of Columbia, Centralia, Hallsville and Ashland. Martin is running on public safety and limited government; Brewer is focused on affordability.

headline: Marist: Sand leads Iowa governor race, Turek edges Hinson
summary: Among Iowa likely voters, Democrat Rob Sand led Republican Zach Lahn 52% to 45% for governor, and Democrat Josh Turek led Republican Ashley Hinson 48% to 45% for Senate. The poll was taken Oct. 8-11.
